author: John Lewis Krimmel
repository: The Metropolitan Museum of Art; object 12728 in the museum's collection API (isPublicDomain: true), image DT1801 at images.metmuseum.org.
locator: Open-access image DT1801: the dancing couples and the fiddler.
rights_note: The Met's Open Access images of public-domain works are released CC0. Proposed for use only as a reference picture the 1812 figures are judged against; nothing traced or sampled.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (dress research for the 1812 scene). Watercolour of a country inn. Young men in shirtsleeves, red waistcoat or brown coat, red neckerchief, light trousers, tall round hats; young women in high-waisted gowns (blue, yellow) with red neckerchiefs crossed over the bosom, one in a bonnet trimmed green; a Black fiddler in a green coat and round hat; an older seated woman in a cap.
note: Proposed for the 1812 dress reference sets; not a Chicago or Fort Dearborn record. Added for the 1812 women's dress (T-3464 dress build, tools/human_women_1812.py) from docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/dress.json.
what_it_supplies: rural working and holiday dress of men and women 1811-1813: shirtsleeves and waistcoats, round hats, high-waisted gowns with neckerchiefs, a bonnet
